trajectory: User is considering a U.S. green card and has asked about eligibility, filing steps, timelines, common mistakes, finances, and what happens after submitting a petition. Their parents have lived with them in the U.S. for about six months, help with chores/cooking/English, and are not working; they may be dependent on the user. User wonders whether parents’ income and expenses must be included. Important nuance: eligibility and required financial evidence depend on petition category, immigrant status, and whether parents are applicants/beneficiaries or merely U.S. residents. Form I-864 and the 125% Federal Poverty Guidelines generally concern the qualifying petitioner/sponsor and sponsored immigrants—not every co-resident family member. Their expenses may still be relevant evidence of available household resources. After filing, typical steps include USCIS receipt, biometrics, background checks, possible RFE, interview, medical exam, decision, and oath ceremony if adjustment of status; consular processing differs abroad. Processing times vary. Advise consulting an immigration attorney for case-specific advice, especially regarding undocumented or otherwise irregular parents.
